notes: Corrected: the accepted alignment put the copula shall be on דֶּגֶל, but in דֶּגֶל מַחֲנֵה רְאוּבֵן תֵּימָנָה the definite construct phrase is the subject and the directional is the predicate, so rule 20 sends the copula to the predicate and rule 49 puts it on the locative marker that holds the English On. Rule 20 warns in terms that the copula stands beside the subject in exactly these cases and that the Hebrew, not the English word order, decides.

This brings the verse into line with 2.20, where the same verbless shape gives the copula to the prepositional predicate עָלָיו and leaves מַטֵּה only its own English; 2.3 is the other case, where the participial phrase is the subject and the standard-phrase the predicate.
The alternative of placing shall be on תֵּימָן's own unit, headed south, is named in the s005 note.
